goal: the two ABSENT operators, and the model that made them ABSENT

the_cap.why_env: so the next wave to meet the cap does not have to rebuild the compiler to test whether the cap is the problem
the_cap.discipline: W823's rule -- raise on a measured slope and a known largest design, never because one design failed

the_documented_slope_was_wrong.consequence: at 21 ms/LUT a 600 s cap appears to buy 28600 LUT; at the rates actually seen it buys 11800. Both timed-out designs were never going to fit, and were reported ABSENT -- which reads like a property of the design.

gft_xorpercep.note: lower bound -- killed at the cap

and_the_slope_is_not_a_slope.spread: at least 1.9x, and NOT monotone in LUT count: the 15946-LUT design is the FASTEST per LUT and the 7851-LUT design is slower than it
and_the_slope_is_not_a_slope.conclusion: place-and-route time per LUT is a property of the design's structure, not of its size. A single slope cannot size a cap; the worst observed rate can, and even then it is a bet.

results.verdict: PASS -- reaches the die for the first time with all four clauses real
results.note: the previous run died at 600.10 s with 16188 LUT. This one took 536.85 s with 15946. The old ABSENT was marginal, not structural.

results.verdict: ABSENT still -- killed at the 1800 s cap
results.note: timing PASSES (1.85 MHz against 1.11). It needs more than 62.9 ms/LUT, worse than any completed build on this bench.

instrument: tri slope -- re-derives the rate from every record carrying both LUT and pnr_s, reports the SPREAD, and sizes caps on the worst rate rather than the average

environment.rebuild: t27c rebuilt in 5m50s after W986 reclaimed disk by deleting target/release/deps

schema_note: W989: a canonical, machine-readable list of every die read in this record. The records grew ad-hoc schemas over twenty waves and `tri table` could place only 10 of 38 reads; this key is the fix, and new records must carry it.
